closing_line: Try Argon on one representative coding task, then judge the reviewed result and cost before changing models.

items.headline: Gemini 4 Argon is now open through the paid Gemini API for real coding evaluations.
items.what_changed: On October 13, Google moved Argon from limited early access to public paid Gemini API availability.
items.why_it_matters: Builders can now compare Argon with an existing model on the same complex code task before changing production settings.
items.who_should_care: Developers evaluating frontier models for multi-file coding work.

walkthrough.use_case: Decide whether Gemini 4 Argon is worth testing for a representative multi-file refactor or debugging task.
walkthrough.steps:
Confirm that your Gemini API project has paid access.
Select the documented model ID gemini-4-argon.
Use a non-sensitive repository and the same task instructions, tests and review rubric as your existing model.
Review the patch, test results, errors and token use before deciding whether to switch.
walkthrough.availability: Public through the paid Gemini API; not on its free tier. Google's introductory standard price runs through November 30, 2026.
walkthrough.limitations: Documented evaluation plan only. We did not call Argon, measure code quality or verify Google's benchmark and engineering claims independently.
walkthrough.evidence_label: Google's October 13 release and API pricing reviewed; no live model call or benchmark by AI Daily Diff.

youtube_description:
Gemini 4 Argon became available through the paid Gemini API on October 13, after Google's earlier limited-access announcement. This builder briefing explains how to evaluate the new model on a complex coding task before switching your workflow.

- Use Google's documented model ID, gemini-4-argon, in an eligible paid API project.
- Run the same multi-file task with your current model and Argon, then review correctness, tests and token cost.
- Standard API pricing starts at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens through November 30, 2026; Google lists higher prices from December 1.
- Google's engineering and benchmark results are vendor claims, not measurements from this channel. This video reviews the documented release; we did not run Argon live.
